summary: Configured 1GB (>512MB) compressed zram swap on node1 (RHEL7, lzo algorithm) with priority 100, which supersedes the existing 2GB disk-backed swap (/dev/vda2, priority -2). Implemented via /etc/modprobe.d/zram.conf (num_devices=1), /etc/modules-load.d/zram.conf, /usr/local/sbin/zram-init.sh, and a systemd oneshot unit zram-swap.service enabled at boot. Verified under real memory pressure (tmpfs fill) that swapped pages land exclusively on zram0, not the disk partition. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-reboot boot_id and healthy zram state, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until SSH returned, confirmed a changed boot_id (2fc81aed... -> 71a394c9...), and verified zram-swap.service was active/enabled with a fresh 1GB zram0 swap device present post-boot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/kernel/existing swap and confirmed root cause (missing modinfo/swapon in default PATH, use of sudo full paths)
Loaded zram kernel module and diagnosed zram0 device creation requiring num_devices=1 parameter
Created /etc/modules-load.d/zram.conf to load zram at boot
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/zram-init.sh to size zram0 to 1G with lzo compression, mkswap, and swapon with priority 100
Created and enabled /etc/systemd/system/zram-swap.service (oneshot, WantedBy swap.target and multi-user.target)
Started the service and confirmed /proc/swaps shows zram0 at priority 100 above disk swap at -2
Generated real memory pressure via oversized tmpfs (/dev/shm) writes and confirmed swap usage occurred entirely on zram0 (528M used) with 0 usage on disk swap
Cleaned up test tmpfs files and restored /dev/shm size
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and zram swap health baseline
Issued `sudo shutdown -r now` in background so the exec call could return before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified new boot_id differs from baseline, proving an actual restart
Verified zram-swap.service is active/enabled and /dev/zram0 is present as a 1G swap device with priority 100 post-reboot

evidence.requirement: At least 512MB compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured
evidence.summary: zram module loaded, zram0 device created and sized to 1G (>512MB) with lzo compression via zram-init.sh, swapon succeeded

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: /proc/swaps shows zram0 priority 100 vs disk /dev/vda2 priority -2; under induced memory pressure, 528M of swap usage landed entirely on zram0 with 0 usage on the disk partition, proving preference in practice

evidence.requirement: zram swap active and enabled at boot (persists across reboot)
evidence.summary: zram-swap.service enabled prior to reboot; baseline boot_id and healthy zram0 captured; reboot acknowledged and connection dropped; post-reboot exec succeeded with a new boot_id (71a394c9... vs 2fc81aed...) and zram-swap.service shown active/enabled with a fresh 1G zram0 swap device at priority 100, no manual intervention needed

Captured pre-restart boot_id/health baseline, issued reboot with async acknowledgement, polled through unreachable window, confirmed changed boot_id post-restart, and confirmed recovered zram swap state and service status
